test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

I came **to know this from** a friend.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original phrase **"came to know this from"** is not incorrect but can be improved for better clarity and natural usage.
 
• The correct phrase is **"came to know this through a friend"**, as **"through"** is the proper preposition when information is conveyed by someone.
 
• Other options either change the meaning or are grammatically awkward.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I came to know this **through**__ a friend."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "to know that from"** – Grammatically incorrect, awkward construction.
 
• **Option 3: "to know of it from"** – Not natural in this context, sounds unusual.
 
• **Option 4: "to know it by"** – Incorrect usage of preposition, doesn’t convey intended meaning.
